text:
alex: Heads-up — new onboarding snag: user enabling structured-output in the sample app reported function-calling responses wrapped in an array, then our SDK schema helper threw an error when jsonMode:true was set.

sasha: ah, can you paste repro steps?

alex: super tiny repro (node):
```bash
npm i @redwood/sdk-sample
node ./examples/structured-array-repro.js
```
config used:
```js
redwood.init({
  jsonMode: true,
  fnCallAdapter: 'schema-chef',
  retry: { enabled: true, strategy: 'auth-refresh' }
})
```
error log:
```
ERROR schema-chef: expected object, got array
    at parseResponse (schema-chef/index.js:45)
    at handleFnCall (sdk/runtime.js:312)
```

devon: my guess: two independent behaviors colliding. The auth-retry wrapper JSON.stringifys the body on retry and our schema adapter expects a parsed object. If the wrapper double-encodes something, we end up with a string that parses into an array node-side and fails strict type checks.

maya: temporary workaround for users: disable retry (retry.enabled=false) or set jsonMode:false and call structuredParser.parse(res.body) manually. Not great UX though.

alex: interesting parity note: Python SDK tolerates single-element arrays and coercively takes the first item; Node enforces type === 'object' and throws. So it's both a parity issue and a retry double-encode issue.

sasha: can you capture the raw wire payload so we know whether the LLM returned an array or client mutated it?

alex: gist with sanitized payload: https://gist.github.com/redwood-repro/ef12a9 — model returned: [{"tool":"get_user","args":{"id":123}}] (an array). Python helper does: coerce_to_object(items[0]); Node helper is strict and errors.

devon: plan: (A) make schema-chef tolerant of single-element arrays by coercing them to objects and emitting a debug log; (B) fix retry layer to avoid re-stringifying already-serialized bodies on auth refresh. I'll open PRs for both.

maya: add an integration smoke test in examples/structured-array/test/repro.spec.js to cover jsonMode:true + fnCallAdapter:schema-chef. Prefer a tiny cross-SDK smoke if feasible (node + python) so parity stays visible.

alex: opened ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SDK-1127 — labels: devex, parity, onboarding. Added repro steps and the gist.

ci-bot: Build scheduled for branch alex/sdk-1127-array-coerce-fix — https://ci.redwood.company/12345

devon: also add telemetry event sdk.coerce.single_element_array when coercion happens so we can quantify how common this is. And include a short DEBUG note in sample-app README.

alex: will include the telemetry, tests, and README note in the PRs. After the fixes land, let's push a tiny change to the onboarding quickstart so new users don't hit this by default. :thumbsup:
